question.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-4{x}_{2}^{2}\le 2{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result,  

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \le 2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=2(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 2.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $2.$ But before we conclude that $2$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=2.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =2(1)^{2}-4(0)^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $2.$
